neighbours.label: the noun that names what is changing, right before shift, gain, loss or change (a paradigm shift, weight gain, weight loss, price change, productivity loss, personality changes), as opposed to the same frames with no such compound
fire: The new law marks a paradigm shift in policing.
Eating out twice a week can mean a five-pound weight gain.
Even a small weight loss helps the knees.
With no fuel price change, costs stay flat.
The region saw a serious productivity loss after the strike.
Warning signs include sudden personality changes.
Doctors noted a rapid hair loss in the patients.
The film shows a sharp mood shift halfway through.
quiet: The new law marks a bad day for police.
Eating out twice a week can mean a big credit card bill.
Even a small garden helps the bees.
With no fuel left in the tank, cars stop.
The region saw a serious flood after the storm.
Warning signs include sudden heavy rain.
Doctors noted a rapid pulse in the patients.
The film shows a sharp knife halfway through.

short: noun before shift, gain, loss, change
notes: '5-10% tip' reached 0.25 on '%' in a probe, perhaps because of the percent.
